title: Union of Utrecht
capsule: The Union of Utrecht was a defensive treaty signed on 23 January 1579 by Holland, Zeeland, Utrecht, and the Guelders quarter — with additional provinces and cities joining through 1580 — forming a military alliance against Philip II of Spain during the Eighty Years' War. The Union coordinated defense, shared taxation, and — unusually — guaranteed freedom of private religious conscience, one of the earliest such provisions in European law. It served as the constitutional foundation of the Republic of the Seven United Provinces, which formally declared independence in the Act of Abjuration of 1581 and received de facto Spanish recognition through the Twelve Years' Truce of 1609.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The treaty text and its signatories are historically documented; representing the Union as a bounded territorial polity is a cartographic schematization of what was a political alliance among provinces whose own boundaries are well known.
